message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference list of the **long weekends** that Canadians can enjoy in 2023.  
(“Long weekend” means a holiday that falls on a Friday or Monday, or a holiday that is observed on the nearest weekday when it lands on a weekend, giving you a 3‑day break.)

| # | Holiday | Calendar Date (2023) | Observed (if different) | Long‑weekend span (weekend days) |
|---|---------|----------------------|--------------------------|----------------------------------|
| 1 | New Year’s Day | Jan 1 (​Sun) | Jan 2 (Mon) | Jan 1 – 3 (Sun‑Tue) |
| 2 | Family Day (Ontario, Alberta, Saskatchewan, New Brunswick, Manitoba, Prince Edward Island) | Feb 20 (Mon) | Feb 20 (Mon) | Feb 18 – 20 (Sat‑Mon) |
| 3 | Good Friday | Apr 7 (Fri) | Apr 7 (Fri) | Apr 7 – 9 (Fri‑Sun) |
| 4 | Victoria Day | May 22 (Mon) | May 22 (Mon) | May 20 – 22 (Sat‑Mon) |
| 5 | Canada Day | Jul 1 (Sat) | Jul 3 (Mon) | Jul 1 – 3 (Sat‑Mon) |
| 6 | Labour Day | Sep 4 (Mon) | Sep 4 (Mon) | Sep 2 – 4 (Sat‑Mon) |
| 7 | Thanksgiving | Oct 9 (Mon) | Oct 9 (Mon) | Oct 7 – 9 (Sat‑Mon) |
| 8 | Remembrance Day | Nov 11 (Sat) | Nov 13 (Mon) | Nov 11 – 13 (Sat‑Mon) |
| 9 | Christmas Day | Dec 25 (Mon) | Dec 25 (Mon) | Dec 23 – 25 (Sat‑Mon) |

**Notes**

* **Boxing Day (Dec 26)** falls on a Tuesday in 2023, so it does **not** create a long weekend.  
* Some provinces have additional holidays (e.g., Family Day on different dates, St. Patrick’s Day in certain provinces, etc.) that may also give you extra long weekends.  
* If you’re planning trips for a specific province, double‑check that province’s holiday calendar for any extra long weekends.

Feel free to copy this table into your holiday‑planning app!
